messages:
Maria: Kicking off a proposal for a canonical quantized-bench protocol (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit). We need a reproducible recipe for warmup, power caps, tokenization, calibration, and kernel-selection logging.

Jon: Agreed. Draft rules: fixed power cap, deterministic tokenizer, both cold-kv and warm-kv passes, and an FP16 baseline run. Keep configs minimal so CI can run them.

Kevin: Important note: first-token cost changes a lot with cold KV and low-precision kernels. We should capture first-token latency and steady-state separately. Observed ~20% first-token penalty on int4 with a cold kv for 13B.

Linh: For tokenizer, lock to sentencepiece v1.0.2 (sha256: abc123def456...). Store token counts and tokenized inputs with artifacts. No on-the-fly tokenization differences allowed.

Maria: Warmup strategy idea: two-phase warmup: 1) prefix warmup to populate KV using representative prompts (helps cold-kv behaviour), 2) stream warmup of N tokens or T seconds to reach steady-state. Propose defaults: prefix = 128 tokens per stream; warmup = 300 tokens OR 30s wallclock (whichever first).

Jon: Also run seq points [16, 64, 256, 1024] and include batch sizes tuned for the model (e.g., batch 8 for 13B). Report median not mean.

Kevin: Calibration sizes: my experiments show diminishing returns past ~10k tokens but quality still improves slightly. Reasonable defaults: FP8: 2k tokens; INT8 and int4: 5k tokens sampled stratified by prompt length. Document the sampling seed.

Linh: Kernel selector logging: runtime must emit which GEMM/kernels it chose per layer or per request (fused vs split, int8-fused, int8-gemm, fp16-gemm). Add a small per-sample line in logs. That helped us track a selector-induced regression last week.

Maria: Perf regression case: after switching selector heuristic to prefer fused kernels for seq<=32, short-seq throughput on 13B fell by ~12%. We need a microbench gate before changing selector heuristics.

Kevin: Repro snippet for the regression we saw:
```
./bench --model=llama-13b --quant=int8 --seq=16 --batch=16 --warmup_tokens=300 --power_cap=240
# before: tokens/s ~ 1480
# after selector change: tokens/s ~ 1305
```

Maria: Power caps: recommend 240W on A100 hosts as the default for comparability. Note: below ~200W some hosts change boost behavior and variance increases. Record power_cap in metadata.

Jon: Fairness: always run FP16 baseline on the same hardware, same power cap, same tokenizer, same batching heuristics. Express perf as % delta vs FP16 median tokens/s.

Linh: Add cold-run metrics (first-token median, p95) and steady-state median per-token. Also attach CUDA metrics: SM util, achieved occupancy, L2 hit rates if available. If SM util <30% for a kernel, flag it in notes.

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot (2026-03-12T17:02:13Z)
```
Model: llama-13b-int8 | seq=64 | batch=8
first-token median: 48ms
steady token median: 2.3ms
tokens/s median: 1150
kernels: prepack_gemm -> quantize -> int8_fused_gemm -> dequant -> softmax
CUDA: SM util 62%, occupancy 45%
```

Maria: Add CSV schema for artifacts so CI can parse results automatically. Minimal columns: model,quant,seq,batch,power_cap,warmup_tokens,calib_tokens,prefix_warmup,first_token_ms,steady_token_ms,tokens_per_s,kernel_choice,sm_util,notes.

Kevin: We'll also store raw per-layer kernel choice histograms to correlate layer-level regressions. Put them under gs://redwood-perf/quant/{run_ts}/layers.json.gz.

Jon: CI microbench suite should include: short-seq cold-kv, short-seq warm-kv, medium-seq steady, long-seq steady. At least one run per quant mode and FP16 baseline.

Maria: Action items:
- Kevin: open INF ticket to lock selector until microbench passes (INF-1234).
- Linh: add tokenizer sha and tokenized sample archives to artifact uploader.
- Jon: add FP16 baseline enforced step in bench script.
- I'll draft a short runbook and a standard bench command.

Linh: Proposed standard command:
```
./run_bench --model llama-13b --quant int8 --power_cap 240 --prefix_warmup 128 --warmup_tokens 300 --calib_tokens 5000 --seqs 16,64,256,1024 --batches 8 --tokenizer spt-v1.0.2 --log_kernels --out gs://redwood-perf/quant/1760871234/
```

Maria: Good. One more: calibration artifacts (calib tables) must be versioned and checksumed and stored alongside results so we can replay quality experiments.

perf-bot: CI job added: quantized-regression-suite -> artifacts posted to gs://redwood-perf/quant/1760871234/

Maria: Thanks team. Once we have canonical runs I'll publish the protocol and a lightweight checker that validates CSV columns and sanity ranges. :thumbsup:
